Environmental risk indication based on current meteorological conditions, not a visual disease diagnosis.
Forecast based on high-resolution meteorological models.
Significant rainfall expected. Ensure field drainage channels are clear to prevent waterlogging.
Strong winds detected. Postpone pesticide spraying to avoid drift and crop damage.
High heat stress conditions. Monitor crop moisture and irrigate during cooler hours.
Low temperatures detected. Protect young nursery seedlings and frost-sensitive crops.
Prolonged humidity above 85%% creates favorable conditions for fungal spore spread.
Rain is expected. Consider postponing irrigation to conserve water and prevent root rot.
High temperatures and evapotranspiration. Provide light, frequent irrigation in early morning or evening.
Moisture and weather parameters are balanced. Maintain regular crop irrigation schedule.
Rain is expected soon. Avoid spraying pesticides immediately before rainfall to prevent wash-off.
Strong winds expected. Avoid spraying during high-wind periods to prevent chemical drift.
Calm winds and clear skies. Favorable window for scheduled foliar spray and nutrient application.
Flowering stage: Avoid heavy overhead watering and harsh chemical treatments to protect delicate flowers.
Seedling stage: Ensure nursery drainage is clear to prevent damping-off root disease during wet periods.
Harvest stage: Plan harvesting during dry weather windows to protect crop yield quality and storage life.
Fruiting stage: Monitor fruit development closely; inspect for fungal spots and rot during humid periods.
Vegetative stage: Good canopy growth conditions. Maintain balanced nutrition and weed-free field borders.
High humidity (%1$d%%) and frequent rainfall create high-risk conditions for fungal and bacterial blights.
Moderate humidity and temperatures (%1$d°C) favor foliar leaf spot pathogen development.
Dry and well-aerated weather conditions minimize fungal and bacterial proliferation risk.
Follow the product label and local agricultural authority recommendations for the correct dose, crop, waiting period, and permitted use.
No chemical fungicides or pesticides are needed for healthy plants. Maintain good hygiene and regular care.
Chemical treatment should be confirmed with a local agricultural authority or product label. Do not apply unverified chemical products.
For severe crop damage or before chemical application, consult your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or agricultural extension officer.
